A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeteorPred study, MP-Bench dataset, and MMLM framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MP-Bench evaluations, module ablations, attention analyses, and error-distribution results in Tables 2–3 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds fine-tuned baseline results, temporal-window experiments, and testing on U.S. NOAA events.

M1.justification: Both versions use parallel DTGF, TGS, and TGCA modules, concatenation, 3D-convolution fusion, and an MLP mapping to the language-model input. Expanded tensor descriptions, zero-padding details, and corrected spatial-mask equations document the existing procedure rather than establish a new architecture or algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 1,000 U.S. NOAA Storm Events samples, extending the China-only evaluation to a distinct geographical and climatic domain through MC-main classification. The original MP-Bench coverage, weather categories, and four QA tasks remain.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares GPT-4o with module-enhanced open models. v2 adds explicitly evaluated, fine-tuned three-channel baseline versions of LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B, Video-LLaVA-7B, InternVL3-8B, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. These are additional comparator configurations in the main comparison, not new backbone names.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Macro-F1 for MC-main and MC-sub, controlled 1-, 6-, and 12-hour window experiments on the 5,000-sample subset, and direct China-trained model testing on U.S. samples matched to MP-Bench test-category proportions across seasons. Existing training hyperparameters largely remain unchanged; newly explained cleaning and implementation details do not establish revised procedures.

E4.justification: v2 adds temporal-context sensitivity experiments and cross-geographical robustness testing. It removes v1's weather-type accuracy radar and normal-weather temporal-stability example, while retaining the module-combination ablation and existing COE error-distribution plots. Thus the analytical coverage changes substantially rather than merely moving into the supplement.

E5.justification: v2's supplementary Experiment Settings first states that results are averaged over three independent runs, and Tables 8–9 disclose seed 42. v1 provides neither disclosure. This does not establish an increase in runs; confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, and statistical tests remain absent.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises reported MMLM scores, including InternVL3 RSW from 39.10 to 70.03 and Qwen RSW from 67.46 to 71.23. Table 3 changes full-module MC-sub accuracy from 36.01 to 47.37. v2 adds baseline, Macro-F1, window-length, and U.S. results, including 64.20 accuracy and 35.18 Macro-F1, and replaces attention findings such as the V-wind peak at 125 versus 500 hPa. These are reported revisions and additions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the TGS mathematical definition in Equations 4–6: the inconsistent indices and mask summation in v1 become an explicit nearest-grid mapping and a position-dependent sum of Gaussian masks over textual locations. This is a limited mathematical correction; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central MP-Bench and three-module MMLM contributions remain. However, the abstract changes 'first large-scale temporal multimodal dataset' to 'first large-scale multimodal dataset,' removing the temporal restriction and broadening the asserted novelty. The introduction's contribution list and conclusion otherwise retain their main scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the physical interpretation of TGCA and DTGF weights, adding synoptic explanations for different pressure-level peaks and category-specific CMA warning-time arguments. It also introduces a claimed performance–computation justification for the 12-hour window, discusses geographical performance decline, and explains rainstorm-to-gale errors through competing signals in compound weather.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the two-hour warning-merging rule, tensor shapes, DTGF first-step padding, nearest-grid coordinate mapping, and the 20-rainstorm sample count for the retained case study. Most hyperparameters remain unchanged, while the explicit LLaMA-Factory/default-settings disclosure disappears. Both versions still promise future code and dataset release.

R1.justification: v2 adds the NOAA dataset reference and four references supporting LLM-based evaluation, removes three appendix references supporting physical interpretations, and expands Table 1 with temporal-alignment comparisons. The broader dataset novelty wording also changes positioning slightly, but the related-work taxonomy and principal comparisons remain.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and substantial experimental discussion, separates baseline and MMLM comparisons into dedicated subsections, and reorganizes the appendix into dataset details, settings, supplementary experiments, physical interpretations, scoring, and case-study sections. QA terminology is expanded and corrected throughout. These changes extend beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the conceptual figure, expands comparison tables with baseline rows and Macro-F1 columns, adds temporal-window tables, and replaces temporal-weight line plots with signed-difference bars. It removes the weather-type radar, relocates the China map alongside a new U.S. map, and substantially rearranges supplementary figures, prompts, and training/evaluation tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support: Table 2 adds relevant fine-tuned counterparts and imbalance-sensitive Macro-F1, while temporal-window and U.S. transfer experiments test assumptions left unexamined in v1. Clearer mathematical definitions and run disclosure further improve assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of weather-type breakdowns and the training-framework disclosure, although unexplained score revisions, absent uncertainty estimates, and missing U.S. baseline scores still limit the conclusions.
